newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi gives 21 pct more industrial loans in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Saudi gives 21 pct more industrial loans in 1996.

text.p: Loans extended by the state Saudi Industrial Development Fund (SIDF), which plays an important role in efforts to encourage the private sector, rose 21 percent in 1996, official figures show.

SIDF chairman Jebara al-Suraisri said in remarks published by the official Saudi Press Agency late on Monday that of 120 loan requests in 1996, the fund approved 109 loans worth 2.43 billion riyals ($648 million).
The fund had extended two billion riyals in loans in 1995.
Suraisri said growth in the industrial sector in the oil-rich kingdom was nine percent in 1996, up from 7.5 percent in 1995.

Saudi Arabia, which says it is committed to giving the private sector a bigger role in its state-run economy as part of efforts to diversify from oil, had in its 1997 budget allocated five billion riyals to four specialised state credit agencies, down from 5.8 billion riyals in the 1996 budget. ($1=3.75 riyals)
